components.notes: Source p. 16 (a common mean, taken to be zero for simplicity; the Theorem 3 hypotheses EX_i=0, X_i<=b) and (1.2), p. 13 (sigma^2 = n var Xbar). The entry has jointly independent X_i, EX_i=0, finite v_i, X_i<=b with b>0, sigma^2 the average variance, Var Xbar=sigma^2/n, no common law or variance, and the non-centred form.

Source Lemma 2 (4.18), p. 23, for every positive h; the extremal law (2.10), p. 16. The entry states the bound, its attainment by the two-point law and the case v=0. The annex writes a complete proof, where the source only points to Bennett.

Source Lemma 3 (4.19) and its proof via f_1, with (4.20)-(4.21) and Jensen (1.9), p. 23, and the tangent-line step of the alternative proof, p. 24. The entry and annex contain all of it, including zero variances.

Source Theorem 3 (2.8)-(2.9) for 0<t<b, p. 16. Also compared: the one-sided bound and the need for two-sided bounds for |Xbar|, p. 16; the t=b limit [sigma^2/(b^2+sigma^2)]^n, p. 16; the Bennett attribution, his notation and his two proofs (pp. 42-3), p. 16; (2.11)-(2.14), pp. 16-17; Bennett better than Bernstein, and (2.12) better than Prohorov (h_1>=h_2 and h_1>=h_3 proved; Prohorov named at annex 148 and body 895); the proof (4.20)-(4.22) and h_1, pp. 23-24; (2.9) read off from (3.13)-(3.16), and the alternative direct proof, p. 24; Bennett's new inequalities and the surveys, p. 14 (body 368-381); and the degenerate b and sigma^2 cases.

Source (2.17), pp. 17-18, applied to Theorem 3; the Doob attribution [7, p. 314] against the reference list, p. 29; and the Kolmogorov analogy via Feller [5, p. 220]. The entry and annex give a first-crossing proof of the maximal bound, the endpoint cases, and a proved Kolmogorov inequality.

Source p. 18: the ratio criterion. Source p. 20: (3.10)-(3.15); rho<x/2 and rho>x/6; the approximation exp(-nt^3/(6b sigma^2)) for small bt/sigma^2 (made precise, with the sigma^2>b^2 caveat); the relation of Theorems 1 and 3 (sigma^2<=-ab, (2.8) increasing in sigma^2, (2.8) implies (2.1), Theorem 1 needs no common mean); and the a-dependent form of (2.9) being no simpler. Source p. 17: the small-lambda agreement of Bernstein and Bennett (expansions of h_1 and h_2). All proved.

Source items compared: p. 14 ((2.1) and (2.8) are the best the method gives but not the best possible) and n. 3 (meaning of best possible, including mu and sigma); p. 16 ((2.8) is the minimum over h under (2.10); equality at t=b); p. 17 ((2.12) is the best bound of the form exp(-tau h(lambda)) from (2.8) and (1.7); attainability at the largest t); and p. 15 n. 4 (the general exponential majorant; the Theorem 3 sentence). The entry has the n=1 example 2/3^(3/4)>4/5 with the sharp value 4/5, the majorant lemma with its sign caveat, and H<=h_1. All proved.

Source Section 5 introduction, p. 24: (5.1) with T_i not mutually independent, the Jensen step, the uncentred form (5.2), bounding each term as in Section 4, the remark on identically distributed or i-free bounds, and the crude-but-useful remark. All present. (5.2) and the centred form are both proved.

Source 5a, pp. 24-25: independent real or vector-valued X_i; (5.3) with n^(r) over distinct r-tuples; (5.4) V with k=[n/r]. The entry uses random elements in a common measurable space and ordered tuples, needs no symmetry, and defines the block averages.

Source p. 25: (5.5) with N=n! and p_i=1/n!; (5.6)-(5.7); the identically distributed extensions with Theorem 1 (n replaced by [n/r], mu=Eg) and with (2.8)-(2.9) (g<=EU+b, sigma^2=var g); and the Kendall example (sign kernel, with tie handling in the annex). All present and proved.

Source 5b, pp. 25-26: (5.8) and its name; the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney example, the count divided by mn with g=1{y<x}; (5.9)-(5.11) with k=min([m/r],[n/s]); (5.7) with this k; and the extension when each sample has a common law (the two laws may differ). All present and proved.

Source 5c, pp. 26-27: (5.12); (5.15) with g* a weighted mean of values of g; (5.16)-(5.17); non-uniqueness, with the half-and-half diagonal replacement; a<=g<=b implying a<=g*<=b, and (5.7) with k=[n/r] for W; the results of 5a applying to W. All present and proved.

Source (5.13)-(5.14), p. 26 (continuous G; nF_n as a count), and the remark on p. 27 that the range of g* is smaller, with a negligible difference for large n. The entry computes the kernel range, the bound, the exact range of g* and the width n/(2(n+1)). All proved.

Source 5d, p. 27: (r-1)-dependence of (5.18); the example S=X_1X_r+...+X_nX_(r+n-1); independence of Y_i, Y_(r+i), ... The entry gives the definition, the residue classes with n_i, and the example. The example's dependence range is verified in the examples entry.

Source pp. 27-28: (5.19)-(5.21); the case n=kr; replacing n_i by [n/r] (the source says this is easy to see; the annex writes the convexity step qL(h/q)<=kL(h/k)); the explicit range bound; and Theorem 1 and (2.8)-(2.9) with [n/r] for identically distributed Y_j. All present and proved.
Source Section 6, p. 28: the population c_1..c_N, samples without and with replacement, and (6.1) mu and sigma^2. The entry states these and allows repeated values.

Source pp. 28-29: Theorem 4 (6.2) for continuous convex f; transfer of the Theorem 1-3 bounds with the (6.1) parameters; EXbar=EYbar and the variance formula; Var Xbar<=Var Ybar as a special case; the proof (6.3)-(6.10); and the n=2 kernel. All present and proved.

A worked-examples entry. The source items it carries are Kendall (p. 25), Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney (p. 26), and the source product example with its dependence range (p. 27). The numerical illustrations and the pairwise-independence failure are the handbook's own. All eight items are proved, and the decimals were checked.

defect_observations.observation: Source p. 15 n. 4 prints the refinement denominator as e^(hnA)-1 with A=n(mu+t). The entry displays e^(lambda n(p+t))-1 without mentioning the printed form. Fidelity note, not a coverage gap.

Source p. 20 says rho(x)>x/6 gives a lower bound for B_1/B_2. In fact it bounds phi from below, and so B_1/B_2 from above. The entry states the correct direction without commenting on the source wording. Fidelity note.

Source p. 23 refers the proof of Lemma 2 to "Bennett [1]", but item [1] of its reference list is Bahadur and Rao. The entry does not record this pointer. The annex mentions it only as "an unread proof from Bennett", which is provenance wording in reader text.

The Kendall example is stated for identically distributed observations. The bound it uses needs only independence, and the source example assumes independent vectors with continuous component distributions. The general statement is covered by thm:p15-one-sample-u-concentration.

The phrase "endpoint qualifications ... transfer" could be read to include the attainment remark of thm:p15-conc-common-range. The annex (722-726) proves only the endpoint extension, impossibility beyond the endpoint, and the degenerate means. Correctness note.
The packet's owned body and annex files are not input by the P15 drivers. They treat 161.3 material only, and no 161.12 or unit verdict here rests on them.
